      "name": "data-description",
      "content": "## Overview

This dataset contains both markets:

- **`developed/`**: the Part 1 data for the established market, 2021 to 2024. It is included so you can reuse and compare your Part 1 work.
- **`emerging/`**: the new market your insurer is expanding into. The insurer has written business there for two policy years (2023 and 2024). At the start of 2025 it takes on a large portfolio from a broker, so most 2025 policies are new business.

**In Part 2 you predict the emerging market only.** Your submission covers every row in `emerging/test_motor`, `emerging/test_buildings` and `emerging/test_contents`.

All data is synthetic. No real person, address or insurer is represented, so you can use it freely with any tool, including AI assistants. Amounts are in a fictional currency unit (CU). The data comes as it would from an insurer's operational systems: in several linked tables, and not cleaned.

## What am I predicting?

For each row in the three emerging-market test files, predict the **expected ultimate claim cost** for that row. This is the risk premium, not the premium charged. It covers:

- all claims with a loss date within the row's period (`period_start` to `period_end`);
- net of the policy excess and of any recoveries;
- including claims not yet reported or settled;
- excluding claims the insurer declined.

The prediction is a total for the row, not an annual rate. A row with `exposure` of 0.5 covers half a year.

Submissions are scored with the D2 Tweedie score (power 1.5). See the **Evaluation** tab.

## Files

Both folders contain the same core tables. The emerging folder adds two files for the commercial premium task.

| File | In folder | One row per | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `customers` | both | Customer | Customer details, shared across all their policies |
| `addresses` | both | Address | Location and property characteristics |
| `weather` | both | Address and year | Annual weather and climate measures for each address |
| `policies_motor` | both | Policy period | Training data for private motor |
| `policies_buildings` | both | Policy period | Training data for home buildings |
| `policies_contents` | both | Policy period | Training data for home contents |
| `claims` | both | Claim | All reported claims on the training policies, as at 31 December 2024 |
| `test_motor` | both | Policy period | 2025 motor policies (**emerging: predict these**) |
| `test_buildings` | both | Policy period | 2025 buildings policies (**emerging: predict these**) |
| `test_contents` | both | Policy period | 2025 contents policies (**emerging: predict these**) |
| `sample_submission` | emerging | Test row | A Part 2 submission in the correct format (CSV) |
| `expenses` | emerging | Cost item | Expense, commission, tax, reinsurance and profit assumptions for both markets |
| `reference_policies` | emerging | Policy | 20 policies for the office premium build-up in your report |

| | Developed | Emerging |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Training years | 2021 to 2024 | 2023 and 2024 |
| Weather years | 2021 to 2024 | 2023 and 2024 |
| Regions | R01 to R12 | E01 to E06 |
| Claims valued at | 31 December 2024 | 31 December 2024 |

Files are provided in Parquet format, except the sample submission, which is CSV.

### How the tables link

Join tables **only within the same market folder**. Customer, address and policy identifiers are unique within a market, but the same value can appear in both markets for unrelated records. Never join a developed table to an emerging table.

Within a market:

- `customer_id` links policies to `customers`.
- `address_id` links policies to `addresses` and `weather`.
- `policy_id` links `claims` to policies. A policy keeps the same `policy_id` across years, so match each claim to a policy row using its `loss_date`.
- `row_id` identifies each test row in your submission. Test `row_id`s are unique across both markets.

A customer can hold motor, buildings and contents policies, and several customers can share an address.

### Policy periods

Each policy row covers one policy for one calendar year, or part of a year. A policy has more than one row in a year if it changed mid-term, for example a new vehicle or a change of address. Rows end early when a policy is cancelled or lapses. `exposure` is the length of the row in years.

## Columns

Identifiers (`customer_id`, `address_id`, `policy_id`, `row_id`, `claim_id`) are text. Read them as text, not numbers.

Where a column differs between markets, the **Market** column says so. A blank means the column is the same in both.

### customers

| Column | Market | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `customer_id` | | Customer identifier |
| `surname` | | Customer surname (anonymised) |
| `date_of_birth` | developed only | Date of birth |
| `gender` | emerging only | M or F. May be used for pricing in the emerging market; not available in the developed market |
| `occupation` | | Occupation. In the emerging market this is free text as entered by the customer |
| `marital_status` | | single, married, divorced, widowed |
| `household_size` | | Number of people in the household |
| `credit_band` | developed only | Credit score band, A (best) to E |
| `prior_claims_5y` | | Claims in the five years before joining, as declared by the customer |
| `licence_points` | | Penalty points on the driving licence |
| `years_at_address` | | Years the customer has lived at their address |
| `customer_since_year` | | Year the customer first took out a policy |
| `email_domain` | | Email provider |
| `marketing_consent` | | Consented to marketing |
| `document_preference` | | email, post or app |
| `previous_insurer` | | Insurer before joining |
| `campaign_code` | | Marketing campaign at acquisition, if any |
| `branch_id` | | Servicing branch |
| `marketing_segment` | | Segment assigned by the marketing team |

### addresses

| Column | Market | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `address_id` | | Address identifier |
| `region` | | Region code: R01 to R12 (developed), E01 to E06 (emerging) |
| `urban_density` | | rural, suburban, urban, dense_urban |
| `flood_zone` | | Flood risk zone, 1 (lowest) to 5 (highest) |
| `distance_to_river_km` | | Distance to the nearest river |
| `elevation_m` | | Elevation above the local river level, in metres |
| `soil_type` | | clay, sand, loam, chalk, rock |
| `year_built` | | Year the property was built |
| `property_type` | | detached, semi_detached, terraced, flat |
| `roof_type` | | pitched or flat |
| `basement` | | Property has a basement |
| `trees_within_5m` | | Trees within 5 m of the property |
| `listed_building` | | Protected (listed) building |
| `bedrooms` | | Number of bedrooms |
| `energy_rating` | | Energy efficiency rating, A (best) to G |
| `solar_panels` | | Solar panels fitted |

### weather

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `address_id` | Address identifier |
| `year` | Calendar year |
| `hail_days` | Days with hail in the year |
| `wind_exposure_index` | Exposure to damaging wind, 0 to 10 |
| `freezing_days` | Days below freezing |
| `dry_summer_index` | Summer dryness, 0 (wet) to 1 (very dry) |
| `wildfire_index` | Wildfire risk, 0 to 1 |
| `rainfall_mm` | Annual rainfall |
| `mean_temperature_c` | Annual mean temperature |

### Columns in all policy and test files

| Column | Market | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `row_id` | | Row identifier |
| `policy_id` | | Policy identifier, constant across years |
| `customer_id` | | Policyholder |
| `address_id` | | Insured address (for motor, the policyholder's home address) |
| `period_start`, `period_end` | | First and last day covered by the row |
| `exposure` | | Length of the row in years |
| `voluntary_excess` | | Excess chosen by the customer: 0, 250, 500 or 1,000 CU |
| `compulsory_excess` | | Excess set by the insurer |
| `channel` | | Sales channel: direct, comparison_site, broker |
| `payment_method` | | annual or monthly |
| `missed_payments_12m` | | Missed instalments in the previous 12 months |
| `new_business` | | First policy year with the insurer |
| `renewal_count` | | Number of previous renewals |
| `days_quote_to_inception` | | Days between quote and the start of cover |
| `discount_applied` | | Discount given on the premium |
| `written_premium` | | Premium charged under the insurer's current pricing |
| `customer_service_contacts` | | Contacts with customer service |
| `renewal_decision` | | Training files only: renewed, lapsed_by_customer, cancelled, declined_by_insurer, mid_term_change |

### Motor columns

| Column | Market | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `driver_age` | developed only | Age of the main driver at the start of the row |
| `driver_age_band` | emerging only | Age band of the main driver: 17-24, 25-34, 35-49, 50-64, 65+ |
| `years_licensed` | | Years the main driver has held a licence |
| `ncb_years` | | No-claims bonus years |
| `vehicle_value_group` | | Vehicle value group, 1 (lowest) to 20 |
| `vehicle_age` | | Vehicle age in years |
| `make_model` | | Make and model code |
| `engine_size_cc` | | Engine size |
| `body_type` | | hatchback, saloon, estate, suv, coupe |
| `transmission` | | manual or automatic |
| `seats` | | Number of seats |
| `vehicle_colour` | | Colour |
| `fuel_type` | | petrol, diesel, hybrid, electric |
| `driver_assist` | | Fitted with driver-assist features such as automatic braking |
| `cover_type` | | comprehensive, third_party_fire_theft, third_party_only |
| `annual_mileage` | developed only | Declared annual mileage (not collected in the emerging market) |
| `overnight_parking` | | garage, driveway, street |
| `vehicle_use` | | social, commuting, business |
| `named_young_driver` | | A driver under 25 is named on the policy |
| `telematics_opt_in` | developed only | Customer opted in to a telematics device (not offered in the emerging market) |
| `telematics_score` | developed only | Driving score from the device, 1 to 100 (blank if not opted in) |

### Buildings columns

| Column | Market | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `policyholder_age` | developed only | Age at the start of the row |
| `policyholder_age_band` | emerging only | Age band at the start of the row: 17-24, 25-34, 35-49, 50-64, 65+ |
| `sum_insured` | | Buildings sum insured |
| `construction_type` | | Developed: brick, stone, timber, non-standard. Emerging (local codes): BRK (brick), STN (stone), WOD (timber), MIX (mixed or non-standard) |
| `occupancy` | | owner_occupied or let |
| `days_unoccupied` | | Longest period the property was unoccupied |
| `smoke_alarms` | | Smoke alarms fitted |
| `accidental_damage_cover` | | Optional accidental damage cover taken |
| `mortgage` | | Property is mortgaged |

### Contents columns

| Column | Market | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `policyholder_age` | developed only | Age at the start of the row |
| `policyholder_age_band` | emerging only | Age band at the start of the row: 17-24, 25-34, 35-49, 50-64, 65+ |
| `sum_insured` | | Contents sum insured |
| `tenure` | | owner or renter |
| `security_level` | | standard, locks, alarm_and_locks |
| `high_value_items` | | Number of declared high-value items |
| `accidental_damage_cover` | | Optional accidental damage cover taken |
| `works_from_home` | | Policyholder works from home |
| `lodgers` | | Lodgers or students in the household |
| `bicycle_cover` | | Optional bicycle cover taken |

### claims

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `claim_id` | Claim identifier |
| `policy_id` | Policy the claim was made on |
| `line` | motor, buildings, contents |
| `peril` | Cause of loss (see below) |
| `loss_date` | Date of the incident |
| `report_date` | Date the claim was reported |
| `status` | closed, open, repudiated (declined) |
| `paid_to_date` | Amount paid so far, net of excess |
| `incurred_to_date` | Paid to date plus the current case estimate for open claims |
| `recoveries` | Amounts recovered from third parties or salvage |
| `repairer_id` | Repairer used (motor damage claims) |
| `third_party_id` | Third party involved (motor third-party claims) |

**Perils.** Motor: `own_damage`, `third_party_prop` (third-party property), `bodily_injury`, `theft`, `glass_hail`. Buildings: `storm`, `flood`, `escape_of_water`, `subsidence`, `fire`, `accidental_damage`. Contents: `theft`, `escape_of_water`, `accidental_damage`, `flood`.

The policy excess applies to all perils, including third-party perils.

Claims in both markets are valued at **31 December 2024**. Some 2024 claims had not been reported by then, and open claims may still develop.

### expenses (emerging folder)

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `item` | Cost item |
| `developed` | Value in the developed market |
| `emerging` | Value in the emerging market (blank if not applicable) |
| `unit` | CU, share of premium, or share of property risk premium |

Items: fixed expense per policy, variable expense, commission by channel, premium tax, catastrophe reinsurance and target profit margin.

### reference_policies (emerging folder)

Twenty 2025 emerging-market policies taken from the test files (same columns, plus `line`). For each one, show in your written report how you build the office premium from your predicted risk premium using the `expenses` assumptions. This is assessed by the judging panel and does not affect the Kaggle score.

### sample_submission (emerging folder)

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `row_id` | Row identifier from the emerging-market test files |
| `prediction` | Expected ultimate claim cost for the row, net of excess and recoveries, in CU (must be zero or above) |

Submit one file covering every row in the three emerging-market test files.

## Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| CU | Currency unit (fictional) |
| Exposure | Time on cover, in years |
| Excess | The part of each claim the policyholder pays |
| NCB | No-claims bonus: years without a claim |
| Sum insured | The maximum the policy pays |
| Incurred | Paid plus outstanding case estimate |
| Ultimate | The final cost of claims once all are reported and settled |
| Repudiated | A claim the insurer declined to pay |
| Comparison site | A price-comparison website |
| Telematics | A device that records driving behaviour |
| Risk premium | Expected claim cost, before any loadings |
| Office premium | The premium charged: risk premium plus expenses, commission, tax, reinsurance and profit |"
    }
  ]
}
